name: movements-020
prompt:
Create beautiful ORIGINAL FORMA exercise art in a clean modern illustrated fitness manual style. Exactly FOUR columns and THREE rows, 12 equal cells, landscape 1536x1024. Each cell white with generous margins; no labels, letters, logos, borders or watermarks. Varied fully clothed adult athletes, charcoal/gray sportswear with a small lime-green accent. Correct anatomy (two arms, two legs), plausible support and weight-bearing, detailed accurate equipment, subtle shadows. Every cell is an EXACT distinct movement/variation matching its description. Show ONE clear representative working position per cell; do not show duplicate athletes, extra limbs, arrows or overlapping phases. Keep the entire athlete and apparatus inside own cell. Never swap freeweights, benches, grips or variations. Read each guide to choose a physically correct pose. Cell positions are mandatory:
Row 1 column 1: Crossbody Leg Swings. Equipment: Bodyweight. Exercise guide: Hold onto a wall or something near you for support. Swing one leg across the front of your body, then back and out to the side. Repeat while slowly increasing your range of motion.

Row 1 column 2: Crossover Reverse Lunge. Equipment: Bodyweight. Exercise guide: Stand with your feet shoulder width apart. This will be your starting position. Perform a rear lunge by stepping back with one foot and flexing the hips and front knee. As you do so, rotate your torso across the front leg. After a brief pause, return to the starting position and repeat on the other side, continuing in an alternating fashion.

Row 1 column 3: Crucifix. Equipment: Specialty equipment. Exercise guide: In the crucifix, you statically hold weights out to the side for time. While the event can be practiced using dumbbells, it is best to practice with one of the various implements used, such as axes and hammers, as it feels different. Begin standing, and raise your arms out to the side holding the implements. Your arms should be parallel to the ground. In competition, judges or sensors are used to let you know when you break parallel. Hold for as long as you can. Typically, the weights should be heavy enough that you fail in 30-60 seconds.

Row 1 column 4: Crunch - Hands Overhead. Equipment: Bodyweight. Exercise guide: Lie on the floor with your back flat and knees bent with around a 60-degree angle between the hamstrings and the calves. Keep your feet flat on the floor and stretch your arms overhead with your palms crossed. This will be your starting position. Curl your upper body forward and bring your shoulder blades just off the floor. At all times, keep your arms aligned with your head, neck and shoulder. Don't move them forward from that position. Exhale as you perform this portion of the movement and hold the contraction for a second. Slowly lower down to the starting position as you inhale. Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

Row 2 column 1: Crunch - Legs On Exercise Ball. Equipment: Bodyweight. Exercise guide: Lie flat on your back with your feet resting on an exercise ball and your knees bent at a 90 degree angle. Place your feet three to four inches apart and point your toes inward so they touch. Place your hands lightly on either side of your head keeping your elbows in. Tip: Don't lock your fingers behind your head. Push the small of your back down in the floor in order to better isolate your abdominal muscles. This will be your starting position. Begin to roll your shoulders off the floor and continue to push down as hard as you can with your lower back. Your shoulders should come up off the floor only about four inches, and your lower back should remain on the floor. Breathe out as you execute this portion of the movement. Squeeze your abdominals hard at the top of the contraction and hold for a second. Tip: Focus on a slow, controlled movement. Refrain from using momentum at any time. Slowly go back down to the starting position as you inhale. Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

Row 2 column 2: Crunches. Equipment: Bodyweight. Exercise guide: Lie flat on your back with your feet flat on the ground, or resting on a bench with your knees bent at a 90 degree angle. If you are resting your feet on a bench, place them three to four inches apart and point your toes inward so they touch. Now place your hands lightly on either side of your head keeping your elbows in. Tip: Don't lock your fingers behind your head. While pushing the small of your back down in the floor to better isolate your abdominal muscles, begin to roll your shoulders off the floor. Continue to push down as hard as you can with your lower back as you contract your abdominals and exhale. Your shoulders should come up off the floor only about four inches, and your lower back should remain on the floor. At the top of the movement, contract your abdominals hard and keep the contraction for a second. Tip: Focus on slow, controlled movement - don't cheat yourself by using momentum. After the one second contraction, begin to come down slowly again to the starting position as you inhale. Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

Row 2 column 3: Crunches With Legs Up. Equipment: Bodyweight. Exercise guide: On your back, legs extended straight up, reach toward your toes with your hands and lift your shoulder blades off the ground and back.

Row 2 column 4: Cuban Press. Equipment: Dumbbell. Exercise guide: Take a dumbbell in each hand with a pronated grip in a standing position. Raise your upper arms so that they are parallel to the floor, allowing your lower arms to hang in the "scarecrow" position. This will be your starting position. To initiate the movement, externally rotate the shoulders to move the upper arm 180 degrees. Keep the upper arms in place, rotating the upper arms until the wrists are directly above the elbows, the forearms perpendicular to the floor. Now press the dumbbells by extending at the elbows, straightening your arms overhead. Return to the starting position as you breathe in by reversing the steps. Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

Row 3 column 1: Curl  - With Shoulder Elevated. Equipment: Dumbbell. Exercise guide: Place elbow so that it is about level with the shoulder. Curl the wieght to your shoulder. Focus on the stretch in the eccentric part of the curl

Row 3 column 2: Curl de biceps con agarre prono. Equipment: Dumbbell. Exercise guide: POSICIÓN INICIAL: Seleccione el peso adecuado en una barra. Colóquese de pie con la barra usando un agarre prono y las manos a la anchura de los hombros. Contraiga el suelo pelvico y el core mientras mantiene su pecho levantado. EJECUCIÓN: Contrayendo los bíceps, doble los codos totalmente mientras exhala. Vuelva a la posición inicial con un suave movimiento mientras inhala.

Row 3 column 3: Curl De Muñeca Con Barra. Equipment: Barbell + Bench. Exercise guide: This is a variation of the flat bench press designed to emphasize the clavicular head of the pectoralis major (the upper portion). By tilting the torso, the angle of the push changes, shifting more tension to the upper chest and shoulders, which helps achieve a more aesthetic, balanced, and three-dimensional development of the torso. 1. Starting Position: Grip a bar with an overhand grip (palms facing up) at a width similar to your shoulders. 2. Position on the Bench: Kneel in front of a flat bench and rest the backs of your forearms on it. Your wrists and hands should extend slightly beyond the edge of the bench to allow for a full range of motion. 3. Eccentric Phase (Lowering): Lower the bar in a controlled manner by extending your wrists toward the floor. At the bottom of the movement, slightly spread your fingers to let the bar roll down a bit, maximizing the stretch. 4. Concentric Phase (Lift): First, close your fingers to secure the bar, then flex your wrists upward explosively but in a controlled manner, bringing the bar as high as possible. Strongly contract your forearms at the top position for one second. 5. Form: Keep your forearms firmly pressed against the bench throughout the exercise; only your wrists and fingers should move.

Row 3 column 4: Curl with kettlebell two hands. Equipment: Kettlebell. Exercise guide: Stand upright and grip the kettlebell with both hands. Perform the elbow flexion motion, starting from a fully extended position until your hand reaches shoulder height. Spread your legs a little for stability and, to perform the exercise correctly, try not to push with your back or body in general. Change the weight of the kettlebell to adjust the difficulty.

cells.title: Curl De Muñeca Con Barra
cells.guideText:
This is a variation of the flat bench press designed to emphasize the clavicular head of the pectoralis major (the upper portion). 1. Starting Position: Grip a bar with an overhand grip (palms facing up) at a width similar to your shoulders.

2. Position on the Bench: Kneel in front of a flat bench and rest the backs of your forearms on it. Your wrists and hands should extend slightly beyond the edge of the bench to allow for a full range of motion.

3. Eccentric Phase (Lowering): Lower the bar in a controlled manner by extending your wrists toward the floor. At the bottom of the movement, slightly spread your fingers to let the bar roll down a bit, maximizing the stretch.

4. Concentric Phase (Lift): First, close your fingers to secure the bar, then flex your wrists upward explosively but in a controlled manner, bringing the bar as high as possible. Strongly contract your forearms at the top position for one second.

5. Form: Keep your forearms firmly pressed against the bench throughout the exercise; only your wrists and fingers should move.
